ref: Diagnose probable critical lower limb ischaemia with foot symptoms / Diagnose probable peripheral vascular disease from foot symptoms
text: The page uses almost the same phrase twice ('Muscle pain in legs or buttocks on exercise' in the red box; 'muscle pain in legs or buttocks' in the PVD flowchart branch) and the file codes them differently: 'Intermittent claudication' for the CLI rule, 'Muscle pain' + finding_site (Lower limb structure / Buttock structure) for the PVD rule. The two check lists therefore contain three different muscle-pain items and the two rules do not see each other's recordings: a nurse who records lower-limb muscle pain (the PVD check item) together with foot pain at rest will not trigger critical limb ischaemia (the urgent diagnosis), and a recorded claudication with generalised foot pain may not trigger PVD (it depends on whether a finding without a finding_site satisfies a site-constrained evidence clause). Suggest the CLI rule accept either form (or the PVD branch add Intermittent claudication), so that the urgent path is not lost on a wording choice.
